picks.name: Adobe
picks.reason: Creative and document workflows look attractively valued against the company’s earnings guidance.
picks.risk: AI competition and the upcoming earnings report could change the thesis.
picks.valueChain: Creative and document workflows: professional tools and customer habits may support durable demand. This is a thesis, not proof of a moat.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess after the September 10 earnings report, or sooner if guidance or subscription demand weakens materially.
picks.evidenceNote: The September 8 judgment used issuer GAAP earnings guidance, not the higher adjusted earnings figure. It has not been recalculated at the latest quote. Leadership transition adds execution uncertainty.

picks.name: Intuit
picks.reason: Its accounting and tax workflows offer a strong franchise at a reasonable earnings valuation in this review.
picks.risk: Slower tax growth, AI competition and lending capital needs.
picks.valueChain: Accounting and tax workflows: recurring business records and filing needs underpin the thesis, rather than generic AI exposure.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess if GAAP earnings guidance falls materially, tax units keep weakening or QuickBooks growth slows.
picks.evidenceNote: The review used issuer GAAP guidance. Lending cash flows need separate analysis; a simple free-cash-flow yield is not distributable owner earnings. Changes to adjusted earnings treatment limit historical comparisons.

picks.name: Autodesk
picks.reason: Design and construction workflows, supported by cash generation, make the valuation interesting.
picks.risk: MaintainX acquisition funding and integration, plus construction cyclicality.
picks.valueChain: Design, build and operate workflows connect software to real construction and industrial work. Retention and integration benefits still need monitoring.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess if post-acquisition cash guidance falls materially or organic growth slows persistently.
picks.evidenceNote: The review considered issuer cash guidance and the announced MaintainX acquisition. Historical free cash flow does not deduct the acquisition purchase price. Cash flow less stock compensation is a proxy, not GAAP owner earnings.

picks.name: Salesforce
picks.reason: Customer records and embedded workflows provide a useful franchise at a moderate cash valuation.
picks.risk: Acquisition-assisted growth and slower cash growth weaken the case.
picks.valueChain: Enterprise customer records and workflows can support AI deployment. AI-labelled revenue is not necessarily incremental revenue.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess if organic growth fails to improve or acquisitions and buybacks weaken the balance sheet.
picks.confidence: Moderate, lower within the Buy group
picks.evidenceNote: Reported growth includes Informatica and guidance includes pending acquisitions. Changed AI revenue definitions and investment gains need care. The cash-flow-less-stock-compensation proxy is not a forecast or GAAP measure.

picks.name: Microsoft
picks.reason: Cloud, developer tools and enterprise distribution support the business, but new buying needs more valuation room.
picks.risk: AI infrastructure spending may not generate adequate cash returns.
picks.valueChain: Cloud infrastructure, developer tools and enterprise distribution provide several routes to customers. Broad reach alone does not prove attractive shareholder returns.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess as cash returns on infrastructure spending become clearer or valuation offers more room.
picks.evidenceNote: The review considered reported GAAP earnings, not only the automated screen’s cash-yield ceiling. Investment-related gains can affect earnings comparability.

picks.name: Fair Isaac
picks.reason: An embedded credit-decision franchise, but policy and debt risks call for a better entry valuation.
picks.risk: Mortgage policy changes, competing scores and leverage.
picks.valueChain: Credit scoring and decision tools sit within lending workflows. Adoption rules and competition can change the economics of that position.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess following material scoring-policy changes, debt changes or a more attractive valuation.
picks.evidenceNote: The review used issuer earnings guidance and reported growth. A separate policy and leverage review is needed before adding exposure.

picks.name: Dynatrace
picks.reason: Observability is useful as software grows more complex; acquisition uncertainty makes adding premature.
picks.risk: Arize integration and dilution from stock compensation or the deal.
picks.valueChain: Observability helps customers understand application performance and failures. Arize could extend that role into AI, but integration benefits are not assured.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess when the Arize transaction’s cash, dilution and integration impact becomes clearer.
picks.evidenceNote: The announced Arize cash-and-stock transaction is not captured by a simple historical cash-yield screen.

picks.name: Datadog
picks.reason: Strong observability growth, but the valuation and stock compensation leave limited cash-yield support.
picks.risk: Growth could slow before shareholder cash generation catches up with valuation.
picks.valueChain: Monitoring and observability benefit from complex cloud systems. That demand does not make any share price attractive.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess after a valuation reset or sustained improvement in cash generation after dilution costs.
picks.evidenceNote: The full issuer release returned an access error during the September 8 review. The indexed issuer release and SEC-linked financial snapshot provided partial coverage, not a full filing audit.

picks.name: Cloudflare
picks.reason: A valuable edge and security platform, but the reviewed valuation demands too much from current cash economics.
picks.risk: Rapid AI demand could justify the premium and make selling too early costly.
picks.valueChain: Edge networking, security and developer services have strategic value. This is a valuation objection, not a claim the platform is failing.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess if exceptional growth translates into much stronger shareholder cash generation, or valuation resets.
picks.evidenceNote: The September 8 judgment compared market valuation with issuer revenue guidance and recent free-cash-flow margins. It is not a short-sale recommendation.

picks.name: Palantir
picks.reason: A strong operational-AI position, but the reviewed valuation prices in exceptional continued success.
picks.risk: Extraordinary growth could continue and make reducing too early costly.
picks.valueChain: Operational AI connects data to business decisions. A useful platform and rapid adoption do not remove valuation risk.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess if sustained growth and cash generation catch up with valuation, or after a substantial price reset.
picks.confidence: Lower — timing risk and partial source access
picks.evidenceNote: The full investor release/PDF was not reliably retrievable during the September 8 review. The call used indexed issuer information and a SEC-linked trailing financial input set. Coverage is partial; this is the most timing-sensitive reduce call.

sources.label: SEC filing index used in financial checks

picks.name: C3 AI
picks.reason: Durable profitable demand remains unproven despite a positive quarterly cash-flow result.
picks.risk: A successful turnaround could reverse the outlook; existing cash gives the company time.
picks.valueChain: Enterprise AI applications need durable customer demand and profitable delivery. An AI category label does not establish either.
picks.reviewTrigger: Reassess after sustained year-on-year revenue recovery and materially lower operating losses.
picks.evidenceNote: The latest issuer release reports positive quarterly free cash flow and substantial cash/securities alongside a significant adjusted operating loss. This is not a bankruptcy prediction. The dashboard’s trailing fields were FMP-only; the call primarily relies on the issuer release.
